<description>
This is just me finding a few more edge cases after #34156 and #34176

The goal of the PR is to handle failures in a controlled way. Just so the process can automatically restore the original wallet without requiring user manual intervention.

The covered cases are:

1. During `DoMigration()`: There are methods that can throw exceptions and abruptly abort the process.
Instead of crashing (GUI) or returning a generic exception, we now will catch and return the error gracefully. This lets the process restore the original wallet automatically.

2. Trying to migrate a wallet in a read-only directory throws a filesystem exception and skips cleanup.
 Now the process will fail gracefully with a clear error msg, and automatically restore the original wallet.

3. Any failure during `MigrateToSQLite` requires user manual intervention.
Now the original wallet db will remain untouched, and only be updated once the sqlite db creation fully succeeds.
</description>

<commits>
edbf3b62a2 wallet: migration, unify watchonly and solvables wallets creation

No need to repeat the exact same code twice.
This will let us introduce new safety checks and improve error
handling for both wallets without the risk of forgetting to
update one of them.

3a9ba874bb wallet: migration, handle exceptions during wallet creation

If creating the watch-only or solvables wallet throws, the migration is
now rolled back like other migration failures: the partially created
wallets are deleted and the original wallet is restored from the backup.

Previously the exception skipped this cleanup, so the user had to restore
the backup and delete the partially created wallets manually.

84a9f48647 wallet: migration, restore backup if an exception is thrown

If MigrateToSQLite or DoMigration throws, the exception previously skipped the
failure handling at the end of MigrateLegacyToDescriptor. The RPC returned the
exception message, and the user was left with a partially migrated wallet and
had to restore the .legacy.bak backup and delete the new wallet files manually.

Catch these exceptions so the failed migration is cleaned up and the original
wallet is restored from the backup automatically, the same way as when
DoMigration returns an error.

cf5e6803f0 wallet: fail migration gracefully on non-writable wallets

Currently, migrating a wallet whose database directory or file
is not writable throws a filesystem exception. Migration
then tries to restore the backup, which also throws again and
the user ends up seeing the raw exception.

Return a regular migration error instead, before the wallet is
modified. The error describes the problem better, and suggests
adjusting the permissions when that is the cause. The wallet
stays as it was, so the migration can be retried once the
problem is fixed without any manual intervention.

b6b2f9f12b wallet: use RunWithinTxn within MigrateToSQLite

Write the migrated records with RunWithinTxn so failures to begin,
write or commit the transaction are handled in one place. A later
commit uses this to return an error instead of asserting.

This is a refactoring except on failure paths that still end in
assert(false): the new database is now closed and deleted when the
transaction can't be started or committed, not only when a write
fails, and the failure is properly logged.

e3a5a48a03 wallet: migration, add MigrationFilePrefix() helper

Move the code that derives the backup file name prefix into a
helper, so the next commit can reuse it to name the temporary
database migration will build, leaving the original database
untouched until the new one has all the records.

The helpers are moved above MigrateToSQLite(), which will call it.

No behavior change.

b8ef499909 wallet: migration, make sqlite creation robust against failures

Currently, MigrateToSQLite loads all BDB records into memory,
deletes the original database, creates the sqlite db in its
place, and writes the records to it. If anything fails after the
delete, the wallet is left partly in sqlite format with legacy
records, and the user has to restore the backup manually.

Instead, build the sqlite db in a temporary directory next to the
original db file, and once all records are written, rename it into
place. For wallet directories, the rename atomically replaces the
original wallet.dat, so any earlier failure leaves the original
untouched. A plain file wallet becomes a wallet directory, which
can't replace the file atomically, so the original file is erased
just before the move.

Before the move, check that no other files of the db, such as a
leftover journal, are at the destination, and fail if one is.
SQLite would otherwise roll a leftover journal back into the new
db when opening it, corrupting it.

Failures once the original db may have been erased or replaced
throw, so the migration restores the backup.

42131a81fd test: migrate wallet located on a different filesystem

399a5a3805 test: migrate a wallet with a leftover journal at its location

Covers the leftover file removal added in "wallet: migration, make
sqlite creation robust against failures". Without it, SQLite rolls
the stale journal back into the migrated db once it is moved into
place, writing pages of an unrelated database into it.
</commits>

+util::Result<void> MoveDatabase(std::unique_ptr<WalletDatabase>& db, const fs::path& dst_path, DatabaseOptions& opts)
+{
+    const fs::path wallet_file{fs::PathFromString(db->Filename())};
+    const std::vector<fs::path> files{db->Files()};
+    db->Close();
+
+    const fs::path dst_file{dst_path / fs::path{wallet_file.filename()}};
+
+    // Other files of this db should never be present at the destination, but an interrupted earlier migration or an
+    // outside process may leave them there. A leftover journal, for example, would be rolled back into the moved db
+    // by SQLite, corrupting it. Return an error rather than guessing whether a file is safe to delete.
+    std::error_code ec;
+    for (const fs::path& file : files) {
+        const fs::path leftover{dst_path / fs::path{file.filename()}};
+        if (leftover == dst_file) continue; // Replaced atomically by the rename below
+        if (fs::symlink_status(leftover, ec).type() != fs::file_type::not_found) {
+            return util::Error{strprintf(_("Error: Unable to move the wallet db, unexpected file %s found at the destination. Move it elsewhere and try again."), fs::PathToString(leftover))};
+        }
+    }
+
+    fs::create_directories(dst_path, ec);
+    if (ec) return util::Error{strprintf(_("Error: Unable to create wallet directory %s: %s."), fs::PathToString(dst_path), ec.message())};
+    fs::rename(wallet_file, dst_file, ec);
+    if (ec) return util::Error{strprintf(_("Error: Unable to move the new wallet db from %s to %s: %s."), fs::PathToString(wallet_file), fs::PathToString(dst_file), ec.message())};
+
+    // Reload db connection
+    DatabaseStatus db_status;
+    opts.require_create = false;
+    opts.require_existing = true;
+    bilingual_str error;
+    std::unique_ptr<WalletDatabase> moved_db{MakeDatabase(dst_path, opts, db_status, error)};
+    if (!moved_db) {
+        fs::remove(dst_file, ec); // Don't leave a db that can't be opened at the destination
+        return util::Error{error};
+    }
+    db = std::move(moved_db);
+    return {};
+}
+
 } // namespace wallet
